# Scientific Background: The Canadian Fire Weather Index

This reading note collects the scientific definitions used in the Canadian
Forest Fire Weather Index (FWI) system and in seasonal climate products. The
references are part of the offline reading material for this calculation.

## Primary reference

Megan McElhinny, Justin F. Beckers, Chelene Hanes, Mike Flannigan, and Piyush
Jain (2020), "A high-resolution reanalysis of global fire weather from 1979 to
2018 - overwintering the Drought Code", *Earth System Science Data*, 12,
1823-1833.

- DOI: <https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-12-1823-2020>
- Full text: <https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/12/1823/2020/>
- XML full text: <https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/12/1823/2020/essd-12-1823-2020.xml>
- License: CC BY 4.0.

## The index family

FWI is a chain of daily calculations. Weather observations update three fuel
moisture codes, and those codes feed spread and fire-behaviour indices:

```text
temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind, latitude
  -> FFMC, DMC, DC
  -> ISI and BUI
  -> FWI and DSR
```

The moisture codes are state variables. A value on one date is the starting
condition for a later date, so a seasonal product must preserve the meaning of
the time axis and the state carried by the calculation. FFMC responds quickly
to weather, DMC represents a slower fuel layer, and DC represents a deep,
long-memory moisture reservoir.

## Daily inputs and units

The standard daily inputs are:

- air temperature;
- precipitation accumulated over the preceding 24 hours;
- relative humidity;
- wind speed; and
- latitude, which affects the day-length factor.

The equations and the xclim API attach physical units to these quantities.
Equivalent unit expressions must represent the same physical experiment. A
station coordinate can be broadcast over the time axis, but state belonging to
different stations remains separate.

## Seasonal calculations

Climate products often select a portion of a time series as an active fire
season. A Boolean seasonal mask identifies the dates used by the active
calculation; the intervals between active seasons are part of the temporal
history rather than a new independent simulation.

The paper describes an overwintering formulation for the long-memory Drought
Code. Let `DC_f` denote the state at the end of an active interval and let
`P_w` denote precipitation accumulated over the dormant interval between
active intervals. The moisture-equivalent quantities are transformed as:

```text
Q_f = 800 exp(-DC_f / 400)
Q_s = a Q_f + b (3.94 P_w)
DC_s = max(400 log(800 / Q_s), DC_min)
```

Here `a` and `b` are model parameters and `DC_min` is the configured lower
bound. The resulting state is used as the starting condition for the daily
calculation in the following active interval. The daily recurrence then uses
the weather observations and the previous day's state.

This formulation is different from restarting every active interval from a
single constant. It also differs from treating all time-indexed observations as
if they belonged to one uninterrupted active run. The interpretation of a
date at an interval boundary must therefore be consistent with the interval
definitions used by the scientific method.

## Downstream quantities

The moisture codes feed BUI, ISI, FWI, and DSR. A change in a long-memory code
can therefore propagate through later quantities even when every returned
array remains finite and has the expected shape. A validation that only checks
for exceptions or NaNs is not enough to establish scientific agreement.

## Supporting references

- R. D. Field et al. (2015), "Development of a Global Fire Weather Database",
  *Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences*, 15, 1407-1423.
  DOI: <https://doi.org/10.5194/nhess-15-1407-2015>.
- Y. Wang, K. R. Anderson, and M. Suddaby (2015), *Updated source code for
  calculating fire danger indexes in the Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index
  System*, Information Report NOR-X-424.
- B. D. Lawson and O. B. Armitage (2008), *Weather Guide for the Canadian
  Forest Fire Danger Rating System*.
- C. E. Van Wagner (1985), *Drought, timelag and fire danger rating*.
- Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index background:
  <https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/background/dsm/fwi>.

All links above are references for offline reading. The calculation supplied
with this task must not depend on a network connection.

==============================
Fire Weather Indices Submodule
==============================

This submodule defines the :py:func:`xclim.indices.fire_season`, :py::func:`xclim.indices.drought_code`
and :py:func:`xclim.indices.fire_weather_indexes` indices, which are used by the eponym indicators.
Users should read this module's documentation and the one of `fire_weather_ufunc`.

First adapted from Matlab code `CalcFWITimeSeriesWithStartup.m` from GFWED made for using
MERRA2 data, which was a translation of FWI.vba of the Canadian Fire Weather Index system.
Then, updated and synchronized with the R code of the cffdrs package.

Parts of the code and of the documentation in this submodule are directly taken from [cffdrs] which was published with the GPL-2 license.

Fire season
-----------
Fire weather indexes are iteratively computed, each day's value depending on the previous day indexes.
Additionally and optionally, the codes are "shut down" (set to NaN) in winter. There are a few ways of computing this
shut down and the subsequent spring start up. The `fire_season` function allows for full control of that,
replicating the `fireSeason` method in the R package. It produces a mask to be given a `season_mask` in the
indicators. However, the `fire_weather_ufunc` and the indicators also accept a `season_method` parameter so the
fire season can be computed inside the iterator. Passing `season_method=None` switches to an "always on" mode
replicating the `fwi` method of the R package.

The fire season determination is based on three consecutive daily maximum temperature thresholds ([WF93]_ , [LA08]_).
In this version, the number of consecutive days, the start and end temperature thresholds and the snow depth threshold
can all be modified.

Additionnaly, overwintering of the drought code is also directly implemented in :py:func:`fire_weather_ufunc`.
The last drought_code of the season is kept in "winter" (where the fire season mask is False) and the precipitation
is accumulated until the start of the next season. The first drought code is computed as a function of these instead
of using the default DCStart value. Parameters to :py:func:`_overwintering_drought_code` are listed below.
The code for the overwintering is based on [ME19]_.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
import warnings
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np


TASK_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SOURCE_DIR = TASK_DIR / "source"
FIXTURE_PATH = TASK_DIR / "fixtures" / "seasonal_weather_case.json"
COMPONENT_NAMES = ("DC", "DMC", "FFMC", "ISI", "BUI", "FWI")


def _load_xclim() -> Any:
    # The historical snapshot predates NumPy's removal of this annotation alias.
    # This keeps that packaging issue separate from the scientific task.
    if not hasattr(np, "int"):
        np.int = int  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    source = str(SOURCE_DIR)
    if source not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, source)
    from xclim.indices.fwi import fire_weather_indexes

    return fire_weather_indexes


def load_fixture() -> dict[str, Any]:
    return json.loads(FIXTURE_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def build_inputs(data: dict[str, Any]):
    import xarray as xr

    coords = {
        "station": data["station"],
        "time": np.asarray(data["time"], dtype="datetime64[ns]"),
    }
    dims = ("station", "time")

    def field(name: str):
        spec = data[name]
        return xr.DataArray(
            np.asarray(spec["values"], dtype=float),
            dims=dims,
            coords=coords,
            attrs={"units": spec["units"]},
        )

    season_mask = xr.DataArray(
        np.asarray(data["season_mask"], dtype=bool), dims=dims, coords=coords
    )
    latitude = xr.DataArray(
        np.asarray(data["latitude"], dtype=float),
        dims=("station",),
        coords={"station": data["station"]},
        attrs={"units": "degree_N"},
    )
    codes = data["initial_codes"]
    initial = {
        key: xr.DataArray(
            np.asarray(codes[key], dtype=float),
            dims=("station",),
            coords={"station": data["station"]},
        )
        for key in ("dc", "dmc", "ffmc")
    }
    return field("tas"), field("pr"), field("rh"), field("ws"), latitude, season_mask, initial


def run_scientific_workflow(data: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
    fire_weather_indexes = _load_xclim()
    data = load_fixture() if data is None else data
    tas, pr, rh, ws, latitude, season_mask, initial = build_inputs(data)

    # Keep the public report focused on scientific values rather than backend
    # warning text.
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
        return fire_weather_indexes(
            tas=tas,
            pr=pr,
            rh=rh,
            ws=ws,
            lat=latitude,
            season_mask=season_mask,
            overwintering=True,
            dc0=initial["dc"],
            dmc0=initial["dmc"],
            ffmc0=initial["ffmc"],

def _active_values(array: np.ndarray, active_mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    values = np.asarray(array, dtype=float)[active_mask]
    return values.reshape(-1)


def _json_number(value: float) -> float | None:
    value = float(value)
    return value if np.isfinite(value) else None


def summarize(outputs: tuple[Any, ...], data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    arrays = [np.asarray(value.values, dtype=float) for value in outputs]
    active_mask = np.asarray(data["season_mask"], dtype=bool)
    expected_shape = (len(data["station"]), len(data["time"]))
    if len(arrays) != len(COMPONENT_NAMES) or any(
        array.shape != expected_shape for array in arrays
    ):
        raise ValueError("scientific output shape does not match the input grid")

    component_summary: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    all_active_values: list[np.ndarray] = []

    for name, array in zip(COMPONENT_NAMES, arrays):
        values = _active_values(array, active_mask)
        all_active_values.append(values)
        finite = bool(values.size and np.isfinite(values).all())
        if finite:
            summary = {
                "finite": True,
                "active_count": int(values.size),
                "minimum": float(np.min(values)),
                "maximum": float(np.max(values)),
                "mean": float(np.mean(values)),
            }
        else:
            summary = {
                "finite": False,
                "active_count": int(values.size),
                "minimum": None,
                "maximum": None,
                "mean": None,
            }
        component_summary[name] = summary

    finite = bool(
        all(values.size > 0 and np.isfinite(values).all() for values in all_active_values)
    )
    return {
        "finite": finite,
        "output_count": len(arrays),
        "output_shape": list(expected_shape),
        "time_steps": len(data["time"]),
        "spatial_points": len(data["station"]),
        "active_fraction": float(np.mean(active_mask)),
        "active_sample_count": int(np.count_nonzero(active_mask)),
        "component_summary": component_summary,
        "seasonal_boundary_profile": seasonal_boundary_profile(outputs, data),

def _active_windows(mask: np.ndarray) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    windows: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
    index = 0
    while index < mask.size:
        if not mask[index]:
            index += 1
            continue
        start = index
        while index + 1 < mask.size and mask[index + 1]:
            index += 1
        windows.append((start, index))
        index += 1
    return windows


def seasonal_boundary_profile(
    outputs: tuple[Any, ...], data: dict[str, Any]
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Summarize observed state and inputs at each active time interval."""
    dc = np.asarray(outputs[0].values, dtype=float)
    mask = np.asarray(data["season_mask"], dtype=bool)
    precipitation = np.asarray(data["pr"]["values"], dtype=float)
    initial_dc = np.asarray(data["initial_codes"]["dc"], dtype=float)
    profile: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    for station_index, station in enumerate(data["station"]):
        windows = _active_windows(mask[station_index])
        for window_index, (start, end) in enumerate(windows):
            previous_end = windows[window_index - 1][1] if window_index else None
            interval_start = previous_end + 1 if previous_end is not None else 0
            interval_rain = precipitation[station_index, interval_start:start]
            previous_dc = (
                float(dc[station_index, previous_end])
                if previous_end is not None
                else float(initial_dc[station_index])
            )
            profile.append(
                {
                    "station": station,
                    "window": window_index,
                    "active_start": data["time"][start],
                    "active_end": data["time"][end],
                    "active_days": end - start + 1,
                    "preceding_interval_days": int(start - interval_start),
                    "preceding_interval_precipitation": _json_number(np.sum(interval_rain)),
                    "start_day_precipitation": _json_number(

    temp_condition_days: int = 3,
    snow_condition_days: int = 3,
    snow_thresh: float = 0,

    tas : ndarray

        start_index = temp_condition_days + 1
    elif method == "LA08":
        # In LA08, the check INCLUDES the current day,
        start_index = max(temp_condition_days, snow_condition_days)

            temp = tas[..., it - temp_condition_days : it]

            start_up = np.all(temp > temp_start_thresh, axis=-1)
            # Shut down when the last X days were all below a threshold
            shut_down = np.all(temp < temp_end_thresh, axis=-1)

        elif method == "LA08":
            snow = snd[..., it - snow_condition_days + 1 : it + 1]
            temp = tas[..., it - temp_condition_days + 1 : it + 1]

            start_up = np.all(snow <= snow_thresh, axis=-1)

def overwintering_drought_code(
    last_dc: xr.DataArray,
    winter_pr: xr.DataArray,
    carry_over_fraction: Union[xr.DataArray, float] = 0.75,
    wetting_efficiency_fraction: Union[xr.DataArray, float] = 0.75,
    min_dc: Union[xr.DataArray, float] = 15.0,
) -> xr.DataArray:
    """Compute the season-starting drought code based on the previous season's last drought code and the total winter precipitation.

    This method replicates the "wDC" method of the [cffdrs]_ R package, with an added control on the "minimum" DC.

    Parameters
    ----------
    last_dc : xr.DataArray
      The previous season's last drought code.
    winter_pr : xr.DataArray
      The accumulated precipitation since the end of the fire season.
    carry_over_fraction : xr.DataArray or float
      Carry-over fraction of last fall’s moisture
    wetting_efficiency_fraction : xr.DataArray or float
      Effectiveness of winter precipitation in recharging moisture reserves in spring
    min_dc : xr.DataArray or float
      Minimum drought code starting value.

    Returns
    -------
    wDC : xr.DataArray
       Overwintered drought code.

    Notes
    -----
    Details taken from the R package documentation ([cffdrs]_):
    Of the three fuel moisture codes (i.e.  FFMC, DMC and DC) making up the FWI System,
    only the DC needs to be considered in terms of its values carrying over from one fire season to the next.
    In Canada both the FFMC and the DMC are assumed to reach moisture saturation from overwinter
    precipitation at or before spring melt; this is a reasonable assumption and any error in these
    assumed starting conditions quickly disappears.  If snowfall (or other overwinter precipitation)
    is not large enough however, the fuel layer tracked by the Drought Code may not fully reach saturation
    afterspring snow melt; because of the long response time in this fuel layer (53 days in standard
    conditions) a large error in this spring starting condition can affect the DC for a significant
    portion of the fire season. In areas where overwinter precipitation is 200 mm or more, full moisture
    recharge occurs and DC overwintering is usually unnecessary.  More discussion of overwintering and
    fuel drying time lag can be found in [LA08]_ and Van Wagner (1985)

    Carry-over fraction of last fall's moisture:
        - 1.0, Daily DC calculated up to 1 November; continuous snow cover, or freeze-up, whichever comes first
        - 0.75, Daily DC calculations stopped before any of the above conditions met or the area is subject to occasional winter chinook conditions, leaving the ground bare and subject to moisture depletion
        - 0.5,  Forested areas subject to long periods in fall or winter that favor depletion of soil moisture

    Effectiveness of winter precipitation in recharging moisture reserves in spring:
        - 0.9, Poorly drained, boggy sites with deep organic layers
        - 0.75, Deep ground frost does not occur until late fall, if at all; moderately drained sites that allow infiltration of most of the melting snowpack
        - 0.5, Chinook-prone areas and areas subject to early and deep ground frost; well-drained soils favoring rapid percolation or topography favoring rapid runoff before melting of ground frost

    Source: [LA08]_ - Table 9.
    """
    winter_pr = convert_units_to(winter_pr, "mm")

    wDC = xr.apply_ufunc(  # noqa
        _overwintering_drought_code,
        last_dc,
        winter_pr,
        carry_over_fraction,
        wetting_efficiency_fraction,
        min_dc,
        input_core_dims=[[]] * 5,
        output_core_dims=[[]] * 5,
        dask="parallelized",
        output_dtypes=[last_dc.dtype],
    )
    wDC.attrs["units"] = ""
    return wDC

    season_mask : xr.DataArray, optional

    season_method : {None, "WF93", "LA08"}

    ISI: xr.DataArray, [dimensionless]
    BUI: xr.DataArray, [dimensionless]
    FWI: xr.DataArray, [dimensionless]

    Notes

    See https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/background/dsm/fwi, the module's doc and
    doc of :py:func:`fire_weather_ufunc` for more information.

    References
    ----------
    Updated source code for calculating fire danger indexes in the Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index System, Y. Wang, K.R. Anderson, and R.M. Suddaby, INFORMATION REPORT NOR-X-424, 2015.
    """
    tas = convert_units_to(tas, "C")
    pr = convert_units_to(pr, "mm/day")
    ws = convert_units_to(ws, "km/h")
    rh = convert_units_to(rh, "pct")
    if snd is not None:
        snd = convert_units_to(snd, "m")

    out = fire_weather_ufunc(
        tas=tas,
        pr=pr,
        rh=rh,
        ws=ws,
        lat=lat,
        dc0=dc0,
        dmc0=dmc0,
        ffmc0=ffmc0,
